I've checked the permissions of the /root/.ssh directory:

The directory has permissions `drwxr-xr-x` which means:
- Owner (root): read, write, execute (rwx)
- Group (root): read, execute (r-x)
- Others: read, execute (r-x)

This is less secure than recommended for an .ssh directory. Typically, the .ssh directory should have `700` permissions (drwx------) to prevent other users from reading its contents.
